newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore pledges to continue to defend Thai baht.
newsitem.headline: Singapore pledges to continue to defend Thai baht.

text.p: Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Thursday Singapore would continue to help Thailand defend its baht against speculators.

"We will continue with what we have been doing, which is to collaborate with the Thai central bank, but as you have seen so far the Thai authorities have managed quite a lot," Hu told reporters on the sidelines of a conference on project financing.
"I think there is no doubt that the present glitch (in Thailand) is a temporary one," he said following the resignation of Thai counterpart Amnuay Viravan.
On May 14, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said it had intervened jointly with the Bank of Thailand in the foreign exchange market to defend the baht against speculators.
MAS, effectively Singapore's central bank, rarely admits intervention in the market.
MAS deputy managing director Koh Beng Seng told reporters two days after the intervention that the move to defend the baht against speculators was effective.
But Amnuay's resignation on Thursday triggered another tumble of the baht in Asia, triggering a wave of hedging against other regionals, dealers said.
Some dealers said news that Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also planned to resign would prompt more selling of baht.
The baht was pushed down to 26.300 against the dollar in late morning, but revived to 25.150/659 at midday.
Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said a new finance minister would be appointed on Friday but kept financial markets guessing as to who it might be.
